title: Tatar — BGN/PCGN 2007 (yaꞑalif-2)
description: BGN/PCGN romanization of Tatar Cyrillic in the yaꞑalif-2 letter set: Ә→ə, Ө→ɵ, Ң→ꞑ, Җ→c, Ж→j, Ч→ç, Ш→ş, Х→x, Г→ğ/g and К→q/k by vowel harmony, У/Ү→w after vowels, И→i (capital İ), Ы→ı, Ь→’.
notes: Vowel harmony (note 3) is approximated letter by letter: Г/К become ğ/q before а о у ы ъ or after а о у ы when no vowel follows, and g/k before ә ө ү е и э ь or by default. Whole-word harmony, the loanword exception, and the back/front choice for Е (yı/ye), Ю (yu/yü) and Я (ya/yä, a/ä) are not modelled: Е gives ye, Ю yu, Я ya by default.
В is w, but v in loanwords (note 2). Only Russian surname endings are detected: word-final -в, -ва, -вич, -вна give v (Шәймиев → Şəymiev). Russian given names such as Владимир come out with w.
Ь is ’ in the table, but the official example Гыйльмиев → Ğilmiev drops it before a consonant; this scheme drops Ь before consonants and keeps ’ elsewhere.
Note 6: after ğ/q, ый is i (Гыйльмиев → Ğilmiev). Note 7: Э after a vowel is ’. Note 8: after и, Ю is ü and Я is a. Ыy for loanwords (note 2) is not detected.
Ё is not in the PCGN table; yo is used.
Zamanalif variant (ä, ñ, ö instead of ə, ꞑ, ɵ) must be used as a complete set; it is not produced here.
Casing workaround: И must capitalise to İ (PCGN inventory) while Ы gives ı/I. И is emitted as a placeholder (U+0269/U+0196) that post rules turn into i/İ.

rules.note: note 4: after a vowel except и, ю; after ъ, ь; word-initially
